headline: TypeScript Template Literal Types Enhance API Safety
summary: Learn how to transform strings from a necessary evil into a type-safe foundation for your APIs, catching errors before code ships.
details: Most TypeScript string handling problems stem from treating strings as opaque primitives, leading to runtime exceptions that could have been caught at compile time. Template literal types allow developers to encode string patterns directly in the type system, ensuring that strings are valid before code is deployed.

This feature uses the same backtick syntax as JavaScript template literals but applies it to the type system. A template literal type defines the shape of strings that can exist at compile time, not runtime. For example, a type like `user-${string}` matches any string starting with 'user-' followed by any content, interpolating types into the string pattern to create constraints.

Union types can be combined with template literals to create finite sets of strings. A type like `/${HTTPMethod}` where HTTPMethod is 'GET' | 'POST' expands to '/GET' | '/POST'. This pattern scales efficiently to hundreds of combinations without manual enumeration, moving validation from runtime to the type checker.

Route handlers are a prime target for template literal types, as route mismatches in production lead to costly 404 errors. By defining route patterns as template literal types, TypeScript enforces them, making route handlers self-documenting and understandable for new team members without needing separate documentation.

Nested paths like /users/:id/posts/:postId can be handled with recursive template literal types. This approach validates each path segment independently, flagging empty segments, double slashes, or invalid characters as errors. This recursive method scales to hundreds of routes with zero maintenance overhead, unlike manual enumeration.

TypeScript includes four intrinsic string manipulation types: Uppercase<T>, Lowercase<T>, Capitalize<T>, and Uncapitalize<T>. These utilities transform template literal types at the type level, eliminating boilerplate string transformations and preventing runtime string manipulation bugs. For instance, they can generate HTTP method types from base actions.

Event emitters and CSS-in-JS libraries are other string-heavy APIs where typos can cause silent failures. Template literal types catch these errors at the type level. For event emitters, define event name patterns and payload types together. For CSS-in-JS, validate property names and unit values, ensuring compile-time failures instead of runtime bugs.
